name: Stedica Surveys
author: Stedica

sections.description:
Stedica Surveys is a survey and questionnaire builder for WordPress. Build a
survey by dragging questions into sections, publish it with a shortcode, and
read the results in your own dashboard. Responses are stored in your
own database.

Everything listed below works in this plugin. Nothing is time-limited, capped,
or switched off pending a purchase.

Building

  • Drag-and-drop builder — reorder sections and questions by dragging
  • Unlimited surveys, unlimited questions per survey
  • 17 question types — surveyor, open ended, closed ended, multiple choice,
    Likert scale, dichotomous (yes/no), rating, number, dropdown, matrix,
    ranking, image choice, demographic, calculated field, photo upload, date,
    signature
  • Conditional logic — show or hide questions based on earlier answers
  • Answer piping — put an earlier answer into a later question’s wording:
    “How was your visit to {answer:q1}?”

  • Option randomisation — shuffle a question’s answer options per respondent
    to cancel order bias, with “Other” and “None of the above” pinned in place

  • Popups, slide-ins and launcher buttons — open a survey after a delay,
    a scroll depth or on exit intent, with page targeting and frequency limits

  • Survey links, QR codes and embeds — share any survey by its own
    address, a printable QR code or an iframe, without building a page
  • 29 starter templates by industry — lead quizzes and scorecards,
    customer experience (NPS, CSAT, CES, post-purchase, restaurant, patient),
    HR, market research, field inspections, education and community
  • Write it with AI, with your own key — describe a survey or quiz, or give
    the address of a page, and get a draft with questions, scoring and result
    screens to check before anything is created; draft result texts in the
    Builder. Works with Anthropic (Claude), OpenAI, Google Gemini or your own
    OpenAI-compatible server, and is off until an administrator connects one
  • Works with AI assistants (MCP) — on WordPress 6.9+, Claude, ChatGPT,
    Cursor and other assistants connected through the MCP Adapter can list your
    surveys, read results and responses, and create draft surveys, as a user you
    choose
  • Question Library — save a question once, reuse it across surveys
  • Survey versioning, with a Go-Live mode that locks schema changes

Keeping responses trustworthy

  • Spam protection — a hidden decoy field, a submission-timing check and a
    per-connection rate limit. No CAPTCHA, nothing sent to any third party, and
    nothing for the respondent to do
  • One response per person — by WordPress account, by browser, or by network
    address, with the limits of each stated where you choose it
  • Response cap — close the survey automatically once it reaches a set number
  • Anonymous responses — do not record which account submitted a response

Collecting

  • Shortcode [stedica_survey id="123"], a Gutenberg block, and an
    Elementor widget
  • Offline capture, switchable per survey — a progressive web app queues
    answers on the respondent’s device with no connection and syncs them when the
    signal returns. Turn it off per survey for anything only ever taken online
  • Offline Sync Monitor showing what is queued and what has landed
  • Progress bar, and save-and-resume for long surveys
  • Photo upload for image evidence, with server-side validation

Notifying

  • Email notification when a response is submitted, to any list of recipients
  • Confirmation email back to the respondent, when the response contains an
    address
  • Merge tags for the survey name, the respondent, any individual answer, or the
    whole response
  • Set defaults once for every survey, then override them per survey
  • Optional Reply-To the respondent, so replying reaches the person
  • Responses collected offline notify when they sync, not silently
  • Webhooks — POST each response to a URL you enter, so another system can
    react to it. Automatic retry if the endpoint is down, and a Send test button
    so you can prove it works before going live

Reading

  • Results dashboard — response counts, completion rate, per-question breakdowns,
    section metrics and a submission timeline
  • Charts — doughnut, bar, stacked bar and a response-over-time line, chosen
    automatically to suit each question type. Every chart carries a matching data
    table, so the figures are readable by screen readers and copyable
  • Net Promoter Score — promoters, passives and detractors, with the score
    and the base
  • Cross-tabulation — break one question down by another (satisfaction by
    region), with row, column or total percentages
  • Individual response viewer — open one response and read it as a document,
    every question in order, with the wording that was on screen when it was
    answered
  • Question drill-down
  • CSV and Excel (XLSX) export of every response
  • REST API for external reporting tools
  • Per-survey backup, restore, and clear-data

Running it safely

  • A Survey Editor role, so people can build surveys without full admin rights
  • Admin audit log
  • GDPR personal-data exporter and eraser, wired into WordPress’s own privacy tools
  • Plugin Health screen that checks tables, capabilities and scheduled jobs

Extensions, sold separately

These are separate products and are not required. This plugin is complete
without them.

  • Stedica Surveys Premium — GPS capture, a geo intelligence map, territory
    and KPI dashboards, risk alerts, and Power BI integration
  • Data Sources add-on — question options populated from an imported CSV or
    XLSX file, with dependent filtering
  • AI Images add-on — product recognition, image recognition and image
    comparison question types

External services

Nothing is sent anywhere by default. Out of the box this plugin makes no
outbound requests: surveys, responses and uploads stay in your own WordPress
database and on your own server.

Three things can send data out, and all are off until you switch them on.

Webhooks (optional, off by default)

If you enter a webhook URL under Stedica Surveys → Notifications, each completed
response is POSTed to that URL — one you choose, not a service we run. The
request contains the survey id and name, the response id and submission time, and
the answers. It does not include IP or device hashes, WordPress user ids, or
internal version ids.

Requests go out through WordPress’s own wp_safe_remote_post(), which refuses
private and reserved network addresses. If you set a signing secret, each request
carries an X-Stedica-Signature header — HMAC-SHA256 of the request body — so
your endpoint can verify it. The secret itself is never transmitted.

Because the destination is yours, its terms and privacy policy are whatever
applies to the endpoint you point it at.

AI writing (optional, off by default)

An administrator can connect an AI provider in Stedica Surveys → Settings → AI,
with their own API key. Until then nothing is sent. Once connected, a request
is made only when someone who can edit surveys clicks an AI button: Write the
draft on Add New, or Write with AI on a result in the Builder.

What is sent: the description typed into the AI box, the chosen kind, number of
questions and language; when a page address is given, the readable text of that
page (fetched by your site with wp_safe_remote_get(), which refuses private
and reserved addresses); and for a result text, the survey’s name, its question
labels and options, and the result’s title, rule and current text. This plugin
never sends responses or respondents’ details. An add-on that uses the same
connection says on its own screen what it sends: the Premium add-on’s
open-text analysis, for example, sends the written answers to the one question
you pick, without names or emails, when you click Analyse answers.

It goes straight from your site to the provider the administrator chose, using
their key; nothing passes through Stedica:

  • Anthropic (Claude) — api.anthropic.com.
    Terms: https://www.anthropic.com/legal/commercial-terms —
    Privacy: https://www.anthropic.com/legal/privacy
  • OpenAI — api.openai.com.
    Terms: https://openai.com/policies/terms-of-use/ —
    Privacy: https://openai.com/policies/privacy-policy/
  • Google Gemini — generativelanguage.googleapis.com.
    Terms: https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/terms —
    Privacy: https://policies.google.com/privacy
  • Your own server — any OpenAI-compatible address the administrator
    enters (for example Ollama on your own network). Its terms are your own.

Licensing and updates (Freemius)

The plugin bundles the Freemius SDK. It runs in anonymous mode: everything
described above works without connecting, and no account, opt-in or consent is
required for any feature of this plugin. Nothing is sent until you choose to
start a trial or activate a licence.

The SDK is used for three things, all optional:

  • the 7-day free trial of Stedica Surveys Premium, a separate paid plugin;
  • licensing for the optional paid add-ons, and delivering their updates;
  • delivering updates to Premium itself, which is not distributed here.

If you start a trial or activate a licence, the plugin then contacts
api.freemius.com periodically to validate it and to check for updates. What is
sent is set out on screen before you agree: your WordPress name and email, the
site’s URL, title and language, the WordPress, PHP and plugin versions it runs,
and whether the plugin is still active. Your surveys and their responses are
never sent. The list of other plugins and themes installed on the site, which
the SDK can collect by default, is switched off in this plugin and never
transmitted.

The Premium Version menu item opens checkout.freemius.com in a new tab. That
is a link you click, not a background request.

  • Terms: https://freemius.com/terms/
  • Privacy: https://freemius.com/privacy/
sections.installation:
1. Install through Plugins → Add New, or upload the ZIP via
    Plugins → Add New → Upload Plugin.
  2. Activate it.
  3. Open Stedica Surveys in the admin menu and create your first survey.
  4. Publish it with the Stedica Survey block, or the
    [stedica_survey id=”123″] shortcode.
sections.faq:
Do I need an account anywhere?

No. The plugin does not require registration and works entirely on your own
site. It contacts an outside service only for the optional features you switch
on yourself (webhooks and AI), each listed under External services.

Where are responses stored?

In your own WordPress database. Nothing is sent anywhere else.

Does the spam protection use Google reCAPTCHA?

No. It uses a hidden decoy field, a submission-timing check and a rate limit,
all handled on your own server. Nothing is sent to any third party, so there is
no external service to disclose and no consent banner to add.

What does “one response per person” actually record?

By WordPress account, it records the account id. By browser, a random value in
a first-party cookie that means nothing outside your site. By network address,
a salted one-way hash — the address itself is never stored and the hash
cannot be turned back into one. Surveys set to anonymous record none of these.

Can respondents answer without an internet connection?

Yes, and it is switchable per survey. Open the survey in the builder and look
under Survey Settings for “Collect responses offline”. When it is on, answers
are stored on the respondent’s device and sync when the connection returns; the
Offline Sync Monitor shows what is still queued. When it is off, nothing is
stored on the device and no connectivity banner is shown.

Surveys created before version 5.0.0 have it on.

Does the plugin work without the paid extensions?

Yes. Everything documented above is in this plugin and is not gated. The
extensions add separate features; they do not unlock anything here.

Do notification emails work with my SMTP plugin?

Yes. The plugin sends through wp_mail(), which any SMTP plugin overrides in
the normal way. If notifications are not arriving, that is almost always the
site’s mail delivery rather than the survey: send failures are written to the
plugin’s error log, visible on Stedica Surveys → Plugin Health.

Can I let someone build surveys without making them an administrator?

Yes — the plugin adds a Survey Editor role with the survey capabilities and
nothing else.
sections.changelog:
5.26.0

AI assistants can work with your surveys, through the WordPress Abilities API.

  • Five abilities on WordPress 6.9 and later: list surveys, get a survey, get
    results (totals, completion rate, result screens, answer counts, averages,
    recent written answers), list responses (up to 100 a call, answers only,
    no respondent accounts) and create a survey (a draft, checked exactly like
    an AI draft on Add New).
  • With the MCP Adapter plugin they appear as tools for Claude, ChatGPT,
    Cursor and any MCP client; they also work through
    /wp-json/wp-abilities/v1.
  • They need the same permission as the Results screen and Builder, run as the
    signed-in user, and creating a survey is audit-logged and blocked in
    Go-Live Mode. This plugin sends nothing anywhere for them.
  • Settings → AI shows what is available and the address to connect to.
  • Developers: Stedica_Builder::insert_survey() creates a survey through the
    same transaction and validator as Add New; filters stedica_surveys_abilities
    and stedica_surveys_abilities_mcp_public.

5.25.0

Write surveys and quizzes with AI, using your own key.

  • New Settings → AI tab: connect Anthropic (Claude), OpenAI, Google Gemini or
    your own OpenAI-compatible server (Ollama, LM Studio, vLLM) with your own
    API key, or define STEDICA_AI_KEY in wp-config.php. Test the connection
    from the same screen. Off until an administrator connects a provider.
  • Add New → Write it with AI: describe the survey or quiz, or give the
    address of a page to base it on, and choose the kind (feedback survey,
    product finder, scored assessment or knowledge quiz), the number of
    questions and the language. You see the draft (questions, options, start
    screen and result screens) before anything is created.
  • The draft is checked before it becomes a survey: only supported question
    types, unique codes and option values, result rules that point at real
    questions and answers, and sensible sizes. It then goes through the same
    validator as every other survey.
  • Builder → Outcomes: Write with AI / Improve with AI drafts a result text
    from the survey’s questions and the result’s rule. Nothing is saved until
    you click Save.
  • Only people who can edit surveys can use it, only when they click an AI
    button, and this plugin never sends responses. See External services.
  • Developers: StedicaAdmin.manualAdd() adds sections to another screen’s
    Manual without replacing it.
  • Developers: Stedica_AI_Connect::json() asks the connected model for JSON
    against a schema; Stedica_Starters::from_definition() builds a survey from
    a starter-shaped definition; filter stedica_surveys_ai_timeout.

5.24.1

  • The Manual on each screen now matches the current layout: the Settings tabs
    in their real order (Tracking and Survey links included), the Popup tab in
    Survey settings, and the survey picker at the top of Survey settings.

5.24.0

Groundwork for A/B tests (the tests themselves are in Stedica Surveys Premium
5.22.0).

  • A survey can be shown as one of several versions, each a survey of its own.
    The version is picked in the visitor’s browser and kept for later visits,
    so it works with page caching, and only the shown version starts a session
    or counts a view.
  • New filter stedica_surveys_survey_split for add-ons that choose the versions.
  • Survey copying is now available to add-ons as Stedica_Builder::clone_survey().

5.23.0

Popups, slide-ins and a launcher button for any survey.

  • New Survey settings → Popup tab: show a survey as a popup in the middle of
    the screen or as a slide-in in a bottom corner.
  • Opens after a delay, after a scroll depth, on exit intent (with a timed
    fallback on phones and tablets), or only on click.
  • Optional floating launcher button (“Feedback”), and any link to
    #stedica-popup-ID or element with data-stedica-popup=”ID” opens it.
  • Target every page, only some pages or all but some (with * wildcards),
    desktop or mobile, and logged-in or logged-out visitors.
  • Frequency limits: at most once per visit, a pause of N days after it is
    closed, and never again after someone answers. Remembered in the browser,
    with no cookie.
  • The survey loads only when the popup opens, so pages stay fast. Campaign
    tags on the page are passed on, so popup responses keep their source.
  • Outcome buttons and redirects inside a popup or embed now open in the whole
    window.
  • Preview on the home page for editors, and a link to the popup settings in
    the Share window.

5.22.0

Share a survey without building a page.

  • Survey links: turn one on and the survey gets its own address, such as
    /survey/customer-feedback/, on a clean page with your site name. Links are
    off until you turn them on, and the survey’s own access, date and limit
    rules still apply.
  • QR codes for every survey link, as PNG (up to 2048 px) or SVG for print,
    drawn in your browser. Scans can be tagged utm_source=qr so they show as
    their own source in the Funnel report.
  • Embed code for other websites: an iframe that resizes to fit the survey.
  • A Share button on All Surveys and in the Builder brings together the link,
    QR code, embed code and shortcode.
  • New Settings → Survey links tab: link prefix, clean page or theme layout
    (classic themes), and whether search engines may list links (off by
    default).
  • Bundles qrcode-generator 1.4.4 (MIT).

5.21.0

Twenty-three new starter templates for the use cases people build most,
29 in all, grouped by industry on the Add New screen.

  • Lead generation & quizzes: product finder, “Which plan is right for you?”,
    marketing readiness scorecard, personality quiz and a graded knowledge quiz.
    Each comes with step mode, a start screen and result screens ready to edit.
  • Customer experience: post-purchase, website feedback, cancellation,
    restaurant & hospitality, patient & client experience and support (CES).
  • HR & people: onboarding check-in, exit interview and job application
    pre-screen.
  • Market research: concept & pricing test and brand awareness.
  • Field operations: workplace safety inspection, property condition report
    and mystery shopper, set to work offline.
  • Education and community: training evaluation, school parent feedback,
    community needs assessment and volunteer sign-up.
  • The template picker has category chips, a search box and badges showing
    what each template sets up (scored, result screens, step mode, offline,
    anonymous).
  • Developers: starters can now set survey settings, a start screen and
    outcomes, and name questions by ref in outcome rules
    (filter stedica_surveys_starters).
  • Freemius SDK updated to 2.13.5.

5.20.0

Know where your respondents come from, and how many of the people who see a
survey actually start it.

  • New Funnel and sources report on the Results page: Views, Starts and
    Completions with start, completion and conversion rates, overall and for
    each source (the utm_source tag, else the referring site, else direct).
  • UTM tags and any other URL parameters you list are recorded with each
    response, together with the referring site and landing page. They show in
    the response view, the CSV/XLSX export, the webhook payload and the new
    {source} and {source:NAME} email tags. Captured in the browser, so it works
    on cached pages and for responses synced later from offline.
  • Fill from URL parameter: any question can start with a value from the page
    address, for example ?store=1042 or ?email=.
  • Analytics events survey_view, survey_start, survey_complete and
    survey_outcome for Google Tag Manager, Google Analytics 4 and the Meta
    pixel, sent only to tools already on your pages and, with a WP Consent API
    plugin, only after consent.
  • New Settings → Tracking tab for all of the above. View counts keep daily
    totals only: no cookie, no IP address, and editors’ previews are skipped
    (an opt-in switch counts them while you test the setup).
  • Privacy: sources are included in personal-data exports and removed on
    erasure. Survey backups and restores include them.

5.19.0

A clearer admin: a grouped menu, two settings hubs and a new Dashboard.

  • The Stedica Surveys menu is grouped under Build, Field insights, Connect and
    System headings, with the everyday screens (Dashboard, All Surveys, Add New,
    Results) at the top.
  • New Settings screen for everything site-wide, in tabs: General (Go-Live
    Mode, Soft Delete Mode, Backup Before Clear, Login Logo), Offline sync,
    Plugin health and Audit log.
  • New Survey settings screen: pick a survey once and set everything for it in
    tabs. The last survey you opened is remembered.
  • The Dashboard now shows a getting-started checklist, 30-day tiles with the
    change against the previous 30 days, a Needs attention list and your recent
    surveys with links to their Builder, Results and Settings.
  • All existing screen addresses keep working.
  • Developers: stedica_surveys_survey_settings_tabs,
    stedica_surveys_settings_tabs, stedica_surveys_menu_layout,
    stedica_surveys_dashboard_stats and stedica_surveys_dashboard_alerts.

5.18.0

Everything a respondent reads can now be translated.

  • The survey’s buttons and messages (Submit, Back, Next, the autosave hint,
    missing-answer and evidence messages, photo, GPS and ranking hints, the
    offline banner and save messages, the skip link and accessible names) come
    from the translatable front-end strings, so a translated survey has no
    English left in it. English stays the default on sites that do not
    translate.
  • The submit confirmation and the offline sync button are translatable.
  • Developers: stedica_surveys_frontend_strings carries about fifty more keys;
    the skip link reads the filtered runtime config.
  • Fix: without the AI Images add-on, product recognition now says the add-on
    is needed instead of returning sample results. Removed an unused photo
    analysis stub that did the same.

5.17.0

Surveys can now work as quizzes and lead funnels.

  • Step mode: one question per screen with Back, Next, an optional Start over
    button and a slide transition, plus an optional start screen.
  • Outcomes: result screens chosen by rules on the answers or by a score range,
    with a default for everyone else. Each can show its text, a button link or
    redirect, the score, advice and the answers given.
  • Quiz scoring: answer options carry points and an optional advice line. The
    outcome and score are saved with each response and appear in exports, the
    response viewer, notification tags ({outcome_title}, {score}, {advice}),
    webhooks and the REST CSV export.
  • The builder preview shows the start screen and, in Test mode, which result
    the test answers reach.
  • Every admin screen has a Manual button with a short guide to that screen.
  • Developers: filters stedica_surveys_resolve_outcome,
    stedica_surveys_outcome_content, stedica_surveys_outcome_payload and
    stedica_surveys_frontend_strings; actions stedica_surveys_outcome_resolved
    and stedica_surveys_survey_deleted; browser events stedica:start,
    stedica:step, stedica:answer and stedica:outcome. The Builder draws sections
    and panels that add-ons register with StedicaBuilderRuntime.

Fixes:

  • Saving a survey no longer loses conditional logic and branching conditions,
    Image Choice images and answer anchors, or the “login required” setting.
  • The REST results endpoint (Power BI / Power Query feeds) returns responses
    again, reads its from/to dates in the site’s timezone, and the survey list’s
    response counts are correct.
  • With Go-Live Mode on, the Builder loads the survey read only and can no longer
    save an empty survey over the real one.
  • The survey’s font and background stay inside the survey instead of applying
    to the whole page.
  • The default button colour is a darker teal (#23807E), so white button text
    meets WCAG AA contrast.
  • Deleting a survey also deletes its uploaded photos and files.
  • Question Library Delete works, the Builder offers to restore an unsaved
    autosave draft again, and Results lists Clear Data backups with Restore and
    Download.
  • Plugin Health and Clear Sync Monitor require the manage_options capability,
    matching their menu and button.
  • Add-on extensions on published surveys load reliably, a photo removed by a
    privacy erase no longer shows as a broken image, and choice questions lose
    the browser’s grey frame.

Older releases are listed in changelog.txt in the plugin folder.

  • AI Images add-on — product recognition, image recognition and image
    comparison question types

External services

Nothing is sent anywhere by default. Out of the box this plugin makes no
outbound requests: surveys, responses and uploads stay in your own WordPress
database and on your own server.

Three things can send data out, and all are off until you switch them on.

Webhooks (optional, off by default)

If you enter a webhook URL under Stedica Surveys → Notifications, each completed
response is POSTed to that URL — one you choose, not a service we run. The
request contains the survey id and name, the response id and submission time, and
the answers. It does not include IP or device hashes, WordPress user ids, or
internal version ids.

Requests go out through WordPress’s own wp_safe_remote_post(), which refuses
private and reserved network addresses. If you set a signing secret, each request
carries an X-Stedica-Signature header — HMAC-SHA256 of the request body — so
your endpoint can verify it. The secret itself is never transmitted.

Because the destination is yours, its terms and privacy policy are whatever
applies to the endpoint you point it at.

AI writing (optional, off by default)

An administrator can connect an AI provider in Stedica Surveys → Settings → AI,
with their own API key. Until then nothing is sent. Once connected, a request
is made only when someone who can edit surveys clicks an AI button: Write the
draft on Add New, or Write with AI on a result in the Builder.

What is sent: the description typed into the AI box, the chosen kind, number of
questions and language; when a page address is given, the readable text of that
page (fetched by your site with wp_safe_remote_get(), which refuses private
and reserved addresses); and for a result text, the survey’s name, its question
labels and options, and the result’s title, rule and current text. This plugin
never sends responses or respondents’ details. An add-on that uses the same
connection says on its own screen what it sends: the Premium add-on’s
open-text analysis, for example, sends the written answers to the one question
you pick, without names or emails, when you click Analyse answers.

It goes straight from your site to the provider the administrator chose, using
their key; nothing passes through Stedica:

  • Anthropic (Claude) — api.anthropic.com.
    Terms: https://www.anthropic.com/legal/commercial-terms —
    Privacy: https://www.anthropic.com/legal/privacy
  • OpenAI — api.openai.com.
    Terms: https://openai.com/policies/terms-of-use/ —
    Privacy: https://openai.com/policies/privacy-policy/
  • Google Gemini — generativelanguage.googleapis.com.
    Terms: https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/terms —
    Privacy: https://policies.google.com/privacy
  • Your own server — any OpenAI-compatible address the administrator
    enters (for example Ollama on your own network). Its terms are your own.

Licensing and updates (Freemius)

The plugin bundles the Freemius SDK. It runs in anonymous mode: everything
described above works without connecting, and no account, opt-in or consent is
required for any feature of this plugin. Nothing is sent until you choose to
start a trial or activate a licence.

The SDK is used for three things, all optional:

  • the 7-day free trial of Stedica Surveys Premium, a separate paid plugin;
  • licensing for the optional paid add-ons, and delivering their updates;
  • delivering updates to Premium itself, which is not distributed here.

If you start a trial or activate a licence, the plugin then contacts
api.freemius.com periodically to validate it and to check for updates. What is
sent is set out on screen before you agree: your WordPress name and email, the
site’s URL, title and language, the WordPress, PHP and plugin versions it runs,
and whether the plugin is still active. Your surveys and their responses are
never sent. The list of other plugins and themes installed on the site, which
the SDK can collect by default, is switched off in this plugin and never
transmitted.

The Premium Version menu item opens checkout.freemius.com in a new tab. That
is a link you click, not a background request.

  • Terms: https://freemius.com/terms/
  • Privacy: https://freemius.com/privacy/
